name: Heavy starting context
why: The first-call prefix (system prompt, tool schemas, CLAUDE.md, skill listings) is re-read on every call; $248 of the $430 is never-called MCP tool definitions.
detect_api: First request tokens minus the user prompt; flag a prefix above 10k tokens, and split it by tools[] size versus system size.
detect_cli: OpenTelemetry/transcript first-call input tokens; /context breakdown; tools[] from prompt_snapshot.
fix_api: Cache the stable prefix with cache_control on the last tool and system block, and defer rarely used tools behind a lookup path (compressed MCP proxy). Class 0 alert first, then class 2.
fix_cli: Keep deferred tool loading on (ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH auto/default), CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, disable-model-invocation on rare skills; remove unused MCP servers (class 3).

techniques.name: Deferred tool loading (tool search)
techniques.how: Tool schemas load only when needed; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto loads upfront until deferrable schemas reach 10% of the window; deferred is the default.
techniques.effect: Example context shows MCP tools deferred at 120 tokens; auto-defer saved about 13.2k tokens in one self-measured setup.
techniques.loses: Needs a lookup step; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false loads everything upfront.
techniques.paper: Anthropic, Explore the context window; bswen, How MCP Tool Definitions Inflate Your AI Agent Token Costs

techniques.name: mcp-compressor (MCP proxy with get_tool_schema / invoke_tool)
techniques.how: Proxy replaces a server's tools with get_tool_schema, invoke_tool and optional list_tools, at verbosity levels full/brief/minimal/none.
techniques.effect: 94-tool GitHub server: 17,600 to 3,900 (low), 2,200 (strong), 500 (max) tokens; quality impact 'almost no' per Atlassian's own evaluation.
techniques.loses: Self-reported by vendor; needs on-demand schema access kept; namespacing prefixes such as mcp__atlassian__*.
techniques.paper: Atlassian, MCP Compression: Preventing tool bloat in AI agents

techniques.name: Tool Attention (ISO score plus lazy schema loader)
techniques.how: Embedding Intent-Schema Overlap score gates tools; a compact summary pool is kept and full JSON schemas are promoted only for top-k tools.
techniques.effect: Simulated 120-tool, six-server benchmark: tool tokens per turn 47.3k to 2.4k (-95%).
techniques.loses: Projection from simulation, not measured on live agents.
techniques.paper: arXiv 2604.21816, Tool Attention Is All You Need (Sadani, Kumar)

methodology: Paired CPS test: same task set with and without deferral or proxy; track task success and tool-call errors next to starting tokens (C:022 evaluates quality with on-demand access kept).
gaps: No measured live-agent numbers for Tool Attention. Hermes' $182 non-MCP share (system prompt, CLAUDE.md) has no specific corpus technique beyond the 200-line target.

name: Cache-write premium
why: Cache writes cost 1.25x (5m) or 2x (1h) base input, so every write pays a premium that only reads repay.
detect_api: Sum cache_creation_input_tokens times price times (write multiplier minus 1); split ephemeral_5m versus ephemeral_1h fields.
detect_cli: Same usage fields via OpenTelemetry cache creation tokens per session; claude -p 'hello' --output-format json shows usage.cache_creation.
fix_api: Use 1h only where reuse gaps fall between 5 minutes and an hour; drop breakpoints nobody reuses. Class 0 alert, TTL change is class 2.
fix_cli: Set promptCacheTtl / CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL for main, subagentPromptCacheTtl for helpers (v2.1.242+); FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 or ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1.

techniques.name: TTL-tier matching (5m vs 1h by reuse gap)
techniques.how: One read repays a 5m write (1.35x vs 2x); 1h needs two reads. 1h fits side-agents running longer than 5 minutes but under an hour.
techniques.effect: Blanket 1h made one deployment's bill 8.6% worse because 98% of reuse landed within about 34 seconds.
techniques.loses: Self-reported blog, one deployment.
techniques.paper: Claude prompt caching docs; dev.to, Your cache hit rate is lying to you. It's the caller mix

techniques.name: Targeted 1h write on the dispatch turn
techniques.how: Write 1h only on the turn that spawns long-running children; dynamic content goes after the stable prefix.
techniques.effect: Dispatch-turn 1h -6.0%; dynamic content after stable prefix -7.6%; all three fixes combined -13.6%.
techniques.loses: Blog measurement, depends on caller mix.
techniques.paper: dev.to, Your cache hit rate is lying to you

techniques.name: Per-caller by TTL hit-rate logging
techniques.how: Log hit rate per caller times TTL tier; a breakpoint nobody reuses costs 25% extra on 5m and 100% on 1h.
techniques.effect: Not measured beyond the examples above.
techniques.loses: Needs a caller label Token Economics must derive.
techniques.paper: dev.to, Your cache hit rate is lying to you

methodology: Replay a week of traffic and compute cost under 5m versus 1h per caller using the 1.25x/2x/0.1x multipliers (A:199); ship only where CPS falls.
gaps: Doc and transcripts disagreed on subagent TTL (C:052); verify with the usage.cache_creation check before trusting it.

name: Cold cache at session and agent start
why: The first call of the main session and of each helper writes the whole prefix, because a subagent's first request does not read the parent cache.
detect_api: First call per derived conversation key with cache_creation_input_tokens above 0 and cache_read 0; gateway cannot see session ids; Token Economics derives a conversation key (prefix hash plus idle gap).
detect_cli: session_id/agent start events plus first-call usage; /usage Prompt cache (main) line.
fix_api: Keep the prefix byte-stable across sessions (static head, volatile content after it) and pre-warm shared prefixes. Class 2.
fix_cli: Use forks (inherit and hit) instead of fresh subagents where possible; keep startup git status stable; sessions share cache only by machine and directory.

techniques.name: Pre-warming with max_tokens: 0
techniques.how: Send a request with max_tokens 0 and an explicit breakpoint on the shared block, same thinking and effort config; billed as a write with zero output.
techniques.loses: Costs a write; wasted if nothing follows.
techniques.paper: Claude prompt caching docs

techniques.name: Persistent per-type static prefix
techniques.how: Give each agent type a stable prefix so children read a warm cache; cwd, date and branch go after it.
techniques.effect: -1.0% alone; combined -13.6% with the other two fixes.
techniques.loses: Small alone; cron/scheduled sessions still ran about 0% hit.
techniques.paper: dev.to, Your cache hit rate is lying to you

techniques.name: Fork and fan-out hold
techniques.how: A fork inherits the parent cache; a workflow fan-out holds all but the first agent up to 5s so they can read its cache.
techniques.loses: Subagents (not forks) still start cold.
techniques.paper: Claude Code docs, How Claude Code uses prompt caching

methodology: Compare first-call cw tokens per helper before and after a stable-prefix change on matched tasks; keep success rate and CPS as the guard.
gaps: No corpus source for a gateway-level conversation key; DevX proposal: derive it from prefix hash plus idle gap.

name: Cache expired after a break
why: After an idle gap beyond the TTL (5m on API keys, 1h on subscriptions) the entire history is rewritten at the write premium.
detect_api: Rewrite (cw above max(5000, 0.5*ctx)) after a gap at or above the TTL on the same conversation key.
detect_cli: Timestamps between calls in the transcript plus ttl; /usage likely-cause text.
fix_api: Choose TTL by gap histogram; keepalive only if the gap fits the crossover. Class 0 alert, TTL change class 2.
fix_cli: promptCacheTtl, idleCompaction=false (v2.1.290+); compact at natural breaks (a cold /compact reprocesses history uncached).

techniques.name: Keepalive crossover rule
techniques.how: Keepalive pings pay off only below a 62.5 minute break (5 x 1.25 / 0.10); TTL runs from request start.
techniques.effect: Rule derived in the source; no field measurement.
techniques.loses: Self-reported blog arithmetic.
techniques.paper: dev.to, Your cache hit rate is lying to you

techniques.name: TTL settings and idleCompaction
techniques.how: Main-conversation TTL is 1h on subscriptions, 5m on API key; promptCacheTtl and idleCompaction control it.
techniques.loses: Needs v2.1.242 or later.
techniques.paper: Claude Code docs, How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: 1h block for long gaps
techniques.how: Use 1h when prompts come less often than every 5 minutes but more often than every hour.
techniques.loses: 2x write cost.
techniques.paper: Claude prompt caching docs

methodology: Histogram of inter-call gaps per key; simulate TTL choices with the multipliers; A/B on a subset.
gaps: No corpus measurement of subscription 1h behaviour beyond the docs.

name: Many agents
why: Each helper agent is a separate model loop with its own context, so fan-out multiplies billed turns and prefix tokens.
detect_api: No session or helper id in API traffic. Derive a conversation key from prefix hash plus idle gap, then count distinct short-lived keys per parent and their cost share.
detect_cli: SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks and transcript sidechains: helper count, turns and cost per parent session.
fix_api: Gateway cap on concurrent derived conversations per parent; route helper-shaped requests to a cheaper model (orchestrator pattern, cheap workers). DevX proposal for the gateway rule.
fix_cli: Set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL or model: haiku on helper definitions; Codex agents.default_subagent_model, reasoning_effort, agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session and rollout_budget.

techniques.name: Orchestrator pattern with cheap workers and fan-out budget cap
techniques.how: A strong planner delegates to cheaper worker models, and total fan-out is capped by a budget.
techniques.effect: 84-98% cost reduction at the worker rate, with a floor cost per delegation and a brief-granularity optimum.
techniques.loses: Delegation floor cost makes tiny tasks net negative.
techniques.paper: Orchestrator / cheap-worker cost analysis (C:012)

techniques.name: Subagent model routing and concurrency settings
techniques.how: Pin helper agents to a small model and limit concurrent threads and rollout budget through harness settings.
techniques.effect: Not measured in corpus as a multiplier; no measured subagent multiplier exists.
techniques.loses: Weaker helper may need retries, erasing the saving.
techniques.paper: Claude Code subagent docs; cache TTL study

techniques.name: Heavier harness with subagents inflates cost
techniques.how: Paired comparison of harness configurations on the same tasks shows added subagent machinery raised cost.
techniques.effect: Cost increased versus the lighter harness (see source for setting).
techniques.loses: Result is one benchmark setting.
techniques.paper: A:051 harness cost comparison

methodology: Paired A/B on identical tasks: subagents on versus capped or cheap-model, compare total cost per resolved task and pass rate.
gaps: No measured subagent multiplier. C:013's 5-10x claim is a vendor blog. Gateway-side detection has no corpus source (DevX proposal).

name: Long history replay
why: Every call resends the whole conversation, so a 100k-plus history is re-read (at cache-read price) on every later turn.
detect_api: Gateway: per request, input+cache_read+cache_creation tokens minus the first request of the same conversation key, flagged above 100k (hermes A1 constant; set from P0 baseline).
detect_cli: gateway signal only; join to session via the x-claude-code-session-id header the gateway receives (C:001) or OTel session.id (A:217).
fix_api: Add `context_management` edits: tool result clearing first (trigger 30-40k, keep 5, clear_at_least 3-5k), compaction as last resort near the window. Both are Class 2, applied only after a paired CPS win.
fix_cli: Claude Code: let auto-compact run, steer it with Compact Instructions in CLAUDE.md or /compact focus; Codex: set model_auto_compact_token_limit and experimental_compact_prompt_file; start a new thread between phases with a handoff file.

techniques.name: Production clearing settings (trigger 30-40k, keep 5, clear_at_least 3,000-5,000)
techniques.how: Cookbook advises lowering the trigger to 30-40k input tokens for production, keeping 5 tool uses and forcing at least 3,000-5,000 tokens freed per clear so the cache rewrite is worth it.
techniques.effect: Guidance only; not measured as a saving in the corpus.
techniques.loses: Defaults of 100,000 / keep 3 fire late; the 30-40k advice has no head-to-head test.
techniques.paper: Memory & context management with Claude (cookbook); Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform

techniques.name: Server-side compaction (compact_20260112)
techniques.how: Beta context edit that fires at `trigger` (default 150K, minimum 50K), summarises the conversation into a typed compaction block, accepts custom `instructions` and `pause_after_compaction`.
techniques.effect: Cookbook: peak 335,279 to 169,164 tokens with a 2,783-token summary; high-level facts kept 3/3, obscure specifics 0/3. Single run. Figures are from A:271.
techniques.loses: Loses verbatim detail; next turn rebuilds the cache; on short sessions the summary call costs more than it saves.
techniques.paper: Context engineering: memory, compaction, and tool clearing (Claude cookbook)

techniques.name: Compact within a phase, new thread between phases (handoff file)
techniques.how: Compact only inside one verifiable phase; at a phase boundary have the agent write a handoff file (docs/plans/*.md), start a clean thread and pass only that file.
techniques.loses: Costs one write turn; loses anything not written to the file.
techniques.paper: Context Management Across Codex Surfaces (Developer Toolkit); Context Compaction Showdown (Vaughan)

methodology: Paired replay on sampled long sessions: arms raw, clearing, compaction; metric cost per successful task with caching on, plus a probe set of high-level and obscure facts after the edit (the A:271 probe design). Sweep clearing trigger 30k/60k/100k.
gaps: No measured dollar saving for history edits in a coding-agent bill: C:024 puts conversation history under 1% of billed cost and caps all visible-token compression near 5%, which conflicts with hermes's 10.5% estimate for this row.

name: Interrupted turns
why: Interrupting a response wastes the output already generated and often forces a re-ask.
detect_api: No corpus source. DevX proposal: streams closed early by client plus follow-up near-duplicate request.
detect_cli: Interrupt hook and Esc events in transcripts, followed by a similar prompt.
fix_api: No corpus source; DevX proposal: alert on abort rate.
fix_cli: Esc keeps everything; /rewind to restore; queue corrections instead of interrupting; Codex agents.interrupt_message and Interrupt hook.

techniques.name: Esc interrupt semantics
techniques.how: Esc stops the turn and keeps all context.
techniques.loses: Kept partial output still costs tokens.
techniques.paper: Claude Code best practices

techniques.name: /rewind checkpoint restore
techniques.how: Restore conversation or code to an earlier checkpoint.
techniques.loses: Loses later work.
techniques.paper: Claude Code checkpointing docs

techniques.name: Queued corrections
techniques.how: Queue a message instead of interrupting; Codex Interrupt hook and agents.interrupt_message.
techniques.loses: Delays the correction.
techniques.paper: Claude Code and Codex docs

methodology: Count aborts per session and tokens discarded; compare with queued corrections.
gaps: Billing of aborted streams has no corpus source.

name: Sessions that never end
why: A new task starts inside an old session, so 20k+ tokens of unrelated prior context ride along on every call.
detect_api: Gateway: derive a conversation key (prefix hash plus idle gap, 30 min per hermes); flag a first-of-task request whose context exceeds prefix plus new prompt by 20k+ tokens.
detect_cli: Hook SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit (C:074) plus transcript compaction count; task boundary from tag or 30 min gap; SessionEnd reason shows clear vs resume.
fix_api: Gateway cannot start a new task itself. Alert with the carried tokens; if a tag or gap marks a boundary, apply tool result clearing at that point (Class 2) or tell the client to reset the thread.
fix_cli: Claude Code: /clear between unrelated tasks (re-loads CLAUDE.md and project context); Codex: /new between phases; recommend a fresh session after three compactions with a structured handoff.

techniques.name: Phase-boundary reset with handoff file
techniques.how: Compact within a phase, open a new thread at the next phase, pass only a handoff file the user reads line by line.
techniques.loses: The handoff is hand-written state; omissions are lost.
techniques.paper: Context Management Across Codex Surfaces (Developer Toolkit)

techniques.name: Three-compactions rule
techniques.how: Each compaction summarises a summary, so loss compounds; after three or more, start a fresh session with a structured handoff. /context shows depth.
techniques.loses: Heuristic from one blog; no threshold study.
techniques.paper: Context Compaction Showdown: Codex CLI, Claude Code and 5 Other Agents; Mastering Context Compaction in Codex CLI

techniques.name: Sub-agent architecture
techniques.how: Give each focused subtask a sub-agent with a clean window; the lead keeps a plan and receives a condensed result.
techniques.loses: Sub-agents repeat startup context (rows 5/13).
techniques.paper: Effective context engineering for AI agents (Anthropic)

methodology: Mine sessions that crossed a task boundary and replay them with a reset at the boundary vs without; compare cost per successful task and first-attempt success on the follow-up task.
gaps: Corpus gives no task-boundary detector and no measured saving from /clear; hermes's 20k line has no stated basis.

name: No clear direction
why: The agent reads and searches broadly before its first edit because the task or target files were not stated, and every result stays in history and is re-billed each turn.
detect_api: Per derived conversation key, count Read/Grep/Glob tool_use blocks in assistant responses before the first Edit/Write tool_use; flag above 15 (hermes constant, no stated basis; set from the P0 baseline).
detect_cli: PostToolUse hook or OTel claude_code.tool_result events (tool_name, prompt.id) give the same count per prompt.id; join to the first edit-tool event.
fix_api: Gateway cannot supply direction. Alert only, then DevX proposal: route read-only exploration turns to a cheaper model (Claude Code does this with the Explore subagent on Haiku, C:072) after a paired test.
fix_cli: Class 3: specific prompts, plan mode (Shift+Tab), an LSP code-intelligence plugin so one go-to-definition replaces grep plus reads, and a codebase-overview skill. Keep the built-in Explore subagent so reads stay out of the main context.

techniques.name: Specific task specification (full spec vs bare user story)
techniques.how: Give the agent a structured spec with the target files and expected behaviour instead of a plain problem description. The study varies spec detail on SWE-bench Verified tasks at three thinking efforts and measures token spend.
techniques.effect: Cutting a full spec to a plain prose problem description raised spend 29.7% and turns 16.4%, 2,700 runs, Kimi K3.
techniques.loses: Prompt sensitivity is task-dependent (13% to 115%); one model; run-to-run spread of x1.34 is unchanged by the prompt.
techniques.paper: Can your AI agent be cheaper? Investigating the effects of task specifications on token spend in agentic coding tasks (Smekal, Stanford)

techniques.name: Code intelligence (language server) plugins plus codebase-overview skill
techniques.how: A language server answers definitions and references directly, so one call replaces a grep followed by reading several candidate files. A skill describing architecture and key directories gives the agent the map up front.
techniques.effect: not measured in corpus (doc states the mechanism only).
techniques.loses: Needs the language server binary on each machine; typed languages only per the doc.
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code), Anthropic; Set up Claude Code in a monorepo or large codebase, Anthropic

techniques.name: Plan mode and Explore subagent isolation
techniques.how: Plan mode has the agent explore and propose an approach before editing, so a wrong direction is caught early. The Explore subagent runs read-only search in its own context and returns a summary, and can be pinned to model: haiku.
techniques.loses: Subagents do not share the parent prompt cache (C:055) and agent teams use about 7x tokens in plan mode (A:215).
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code); Create custom subagents, Anthropic; How Claude Code uses prompt caching, Anthropic

techniques.name: Aider tree-sitter repo map (--map-tokens)
techniques.how: Builds a dependency graph from tree-sitter definitions and ranks symbols with a graph-ranking algorithm to fit a token budget (default 1k), so the model sees structure without reading files.
techniques.loses: Budget is a target not a ceiling: issue reports show 16,000 tokens at --map-tokens 1024; map is doubled when no files are added.
techniques.paper: How to Manage the Aider Context Window and Token Budgets; How to Reduce Aider Token Usage (Tokenade blogs)

methodology: Paired A/B on matched tasks: vague prompt vs specific prompt (C:027 design: repeat each arm, report mean and spread), with and without LSP plugin. Metric: billed cost per successful task, plus reads before first edit. Run 3 repeats per arm because run spread is about x1.34.
gaps: No corpus source measures the cost of exploration itself or a read-count threshold. Kiro has no source in the CLI corpus. No billed saving for LSP plugins or plan mode.

name: Restarting too often
why: A fresh session soon after the last one rebuilds the same context (re-reads files, re-issues setup) at cold-cache prices.
detect_api: Gateway: new conversation key within 3600 s of the previous one for the same caller and project, with cache_creation high and overlapping prefix; cost = calls before the first edit.
detect_cli: Hook SessionStart source (startup/resume/clear/compact/fork) and SessionEnd reason (C:074); gap under RESTART_GAP 3600 s.
fix_api: Class 0 alert. Where the client supports it, keep the cache warm (TTL choice is a Class 2 change).
fix_cli: Resume the session instead of starting anew (the whole conversation resends, unchanged prefix still reads from cache within the TTL); persist state in auto memory or a handoff file; use idleCompaction=false if idle compaction itself triggers rewrites.

techniques.name: Resume a session (cache-aware)
techniques.how: Resume resends the whole conversation; the unchanged prefix still hits the cache within the cache lifetime, one hour on a Claude subscription by default, five minutes otherwise.
techniques.effect: Resume benefit not quantified in corpus.
techniques.loses: After a break longer than the TTL nothing is cached and resume reprocesses history uncached; /compact then costs the most.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching (Anthropic)

techniques.name: Auto memory (MEMORY.md index + topic files)
techniques.how: Claude writes four kinds of notes itself to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/; the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md load each session. Toggle autoMemoryEnabled, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY, autoMemoryDirectory.
techniques.loses: Loaded every session so it is a standing token cost; a wrong note repeats in every session.
techniques.paper: How Claude remembers your project (Anthropic)

techniques.name: Handoff file between threads
techniques.how: Write docs/plans/<task>.md before ending the thread; start the next thread from it.
techniques.loses: Hand-maintained.
techniques.paper: Context Management Across Codex Surfaces (Developer Toolkit)

methodology: Compare matched task pairs started as new session vs resumed/handoff: cost per successful task and tokens before first edit.
gaps: No measured saving for restart avoidance; resume economics beyond the TTL rule are not quantified.

name: Stale tool results carried forward
why: File reads and command output stay in context 30+ calls after use, and are re-read on every call.
detect_api: Gateway: tool_result blocks that remain in the messages array 30 calls after first appearing; tokens (plus image tokens) times later cache-read price until compaction (hermes A5).
detect_cli: gateway signal only (transcript tool_use_id gives the same).
fix_api: Inject context_management clear_tool_uses_20250919 with trigger 30-40k, keep 5, clear_at_least 3-5k and exclude_tools for results that cannot be re-fetched; or gateway-side masking with a rolling window. Both Class 2.
fix_cli: Claude Code microcompact/tool trimming already runs before LLM summary (C:112); Aider: /drop files; Codex: compact within phase. Masking with a tuned M needs harness support.

techniques.name: Tool result clearing (clear_tool_uses_20250919)
techniques.how: Server replaces the oldest tool results with placeholder text once input exceeds `trigger` (default 100,000), keeps the last `keep` (default 3) pairs, skips if `clear_at_least` tokens cannot be freed, and honours `exclude_tools`.
techniques.effect: Cookbook run, one synthetic task: peak context 335,279 to 173,137 tokens. No dollars, single run. Figures are from A:271.
techniques.loses: Invalidates the cached prefix on every clear, so each clear pays a cache write; cleared content is gone unless re-fetched.
techniques.paper: Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform (Anthropic); Context engineering: memory, compaction, and tool clearing (Anthropic cookbook)

techniques.name: Observation masking (rolling window M)
techniques.how: Replace tool observations older than the last M turns with a short placeholder (for example 'Previous 8 lines omitted'); the agent's own reasoning and actions stay.
techniques.effect: SWE-agent, M=10: cost per instance cut by more than half in most setups (Gemini 2.5 Flash $0.41 to $0.18); solve rate not significantly lower. Qwen3-Coder solve rate 54.8% masked vs 53.4% raw.
techniques.loses: Needs re-tuning per scaffold; masking loses at 7 events or fewer (-45% to -149% savings); only +8.6% net on a 9-event average task set.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap: Observation Masking vs LLM Summarization (JetBrains Research); Evaluating Memory Condensation Strategies for Coding Agents in Data-Driven Scientific Discovery

techniques.name: Observation masking vs LLM summarisation hybrid
techniques.how: Combine masking of old observations with LLM summarisation of the turn history rather than either alone.
techniques.effect: Cost down a further 7% vs masking alone and 11% vs summary alone (SWE-agent/OpenHands).
techniques.loses: Adds an LLM call and one more knob set.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains Research)

techniques.name: Garbage-collector view: liveness and write barriers
techniques.how: Clearing is garbage collection with no liveness knowledge; protect results the agent builds on via exclude_tools and write state to memory before clearing.
techniques.loses: Opinion piece; exclude_tools is described as crude.
techniques.paper: Context Editing Looks Like a Feature. It's Actually a Garbage Collector Without Write Barriers

methodology: Arms raw/clearing/masking on sampled traffic; billed cost with caching on, count of cache rewrites caused by clears, and re-fetch rate of cleared files (agent re-reads).
gaps: Cache-aware break-even for clearing (yield vs rewrite) is not measured in the corpus; masking effect at 8-10 events is mixed (C:133).

name: Bigger model than needed
why: Simple tasks and helper calls run on the most expensive model when a cheaper one gives the same result.
detect_api: Classify difficulty per call (simple categories, helper calls) and compare the model used with sonnet-5-5 price delta; gateway needs a difficulty classifier.
detect_cli: Transcript model field per turn and subagent; flag Opus/Fable on simple-category turns and helper subagents.
fix_api: Class 2 after a paired CPS win: RouteLLM matrix-factorization router or FrugalGPT cascade at the gateway; escalate only flagged hard tasks.
fix_cli: Set subagent model (frontmatter or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL), the opusplan alias (Opus plans, Sonnet executes), and availableModels allowlists.

techniques.name: RouteLLM matrix-factorization router
techniques.how: Learns P(win) between strong and weak model from preference data using query embeddings; threshold sets the strong-model share.
techniques.effect: Over 2x cost reduction without quality loss; 95% of GPT-4 score at 50% calls (MT Bench).
techniques.loses: BERT and causal-LLM routers near random on low-data training.
techniques.paper: RouteLLM (arXiv 2406.18665)

techniques.name: FrugalGPT LLM cascade
techniques.how: A scoring function rates each answer in [0,1]; query models in order and stop at threshold tau.
techniques.effect: Matches GPT-4 with up to 98% lower cost.
techniques.loses: Needs a trained scorer and thresholds.
techniques.paper: FrugalGPT (Chen, Zaharia, Zou)

techniques.name: Hybrid LLM router
techniques.how: Predicts query difficulty and routes small or large; threshold tunable at test time.
techniques.effect: Up to 40% fewer large-model calls, no quality drop.
techniques.loses: Depends on difficulty predictor.
techniques.paper: Hybrid LLM (Microsoft Research)

techniques.name: Classifier routing, Cost per task
techniques.how: Cheap yes/no complexity classifier routes between Flash-Lite and Flash; escalate flagged tasks only.
techniques.effect: Router solved 50/50; regex plus length heuristic fell to 70.6% held-out.
techniques.loses: 50 hand-labelled prompts, single runs; routing and caching pull apart.
techniques.paper: Cost per task (Google blog)

methodology: Use PGR/CPT(x%) from RouteLLM: minimum strong-model share to reach a target quality, plus paired CPS on your own tasks.
gaps: Price Reversal (A:069) warns cheaper listed models can cost more (32% of pairs). Router attack risk (A:010). Corpus has no gateway difficulty classifier specific to coding.

name: Fork context duplication
why: A forked subagent inherits the parent prefix, so every fork re-sends the whole parent context.
detect_api: Requests sharing a long identical prefix hash with a parent but different tails; cache_read versus cache_creation tokens in usage.
detect_cli: SubagentStart hook with fork flag; transcript sidechain input tokens versus parent prefix size.
fix_api: Keep prefix byte-identical so forks read cache; avoid forks after the 5-minute TTL lapses. Prefix-stability guard, class 1.
fix_cli: CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 to use a fresh subagent, with omitClaudeMd and a short brief; keep the warm cache alive.

techniques.name: Fork subagent reads the parent prompt cache
techniques.how: Fork shares the parent prefix so the excess is cache-read priced; a non-fork subagent starts its own cache.
techniques.effect: Excess is cheap unless the cache is dead.
techniques.loses: After the 5-minute cliff the fork pays full creation price.
techniques.paper: Claude Code subagent docs; prompt cache TTL analysis

techniques.name: Cache TTL study (stable prefix, dynamic content last)
techniques.how: Measured waits against the 5-minute TTL; 96% of waits fall in the cliff. Stable per-type prefix and dynamic content after it.
techniques.effect: Combined fixes -13.6%; stable prefix -1.0%; dynamic after prefix -7.6%; blanket 1h TTL +8.6% worse.
techniques.loses: Blanket 1h TTL costs more.
techniques.paper: C:052 prompt cache analysis

techniques.name: Sub-agent context isolation
techniques.how: Run exploration in a fresh context and return a 1,000-2,000 token summary.
techniques.effect: Net saving not measured in corpus.
techniques.loses: Isolation cost can exceed the benefit for small tasks.
techniques.paper: A:084 context engineering guide

methodology: Compare fork on versus off on matched tasks measuring cache-read share, total cost and pass rate.
gaps: Net saving from subagent isolation is not in the corpus.

name: Large tool-call arguments
why: Long plans, whole-file writes and big shell heredocs are billed as output tokens at the higher output rate and then stay in history as input on every later turn.
detect_api: In assistant response content, tokenise json of each tool_use input (non-edit, non-agent tools); flag above 1,000 tokens (hermes A66). Count against usage.output_tokens.
detect_cli: Gateway signal only for size; OTel tool_result gives tool_name and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 adds parameters (C:002).
fix_api: Use the provider text_editor tool and token-efficient tool use where the model supports it; once the context passes a trigger, clear old tool calls with clear_tool_inputs=true in context editing.
fix_cli: Aider: use edit format diff or udiff, not whole. Claude Code: skill or rule to persist and revise scripts instead of regenerating variants (DevSkills principle). Context editing is API-only, no CLI flag in corpus.

techniques.name: Aider edit formats (diff / udiff vs whole)
techniques.how: diff returns search/replace blocks and udiff a simplified unified diff, so output scales with the change, while whole returns a full copy of every changed file.
techniques.effect: not measured in corpus (blog asserts the whole default can outweigh all other costs).
techniques.loses: Weaker models fail diff formats; blog says use whole only when the model cannot do better.
techniques.paper: How to Reduce Aider Token Usage (Tokenade blog)

techniques.name: Token-efficient tool use beta and text_editor tool
techniques.how: Header token-efficient-tools-2025-02-19 makes tool calls shorter in output tokens. The text_editor tool makes targeted edits to portions of a file instead of rewriting it.
techniques.effect: Up to 70% output-token cut, 14% average, vendor-reported, Claude 3.7 Sonnet only.
techniques.loses: Limited to one model generation in the source; vendor numbers, no method.
techniques.paper: Token-saving updates on the Anthropic API, Anthropic

techniques.name: Context editing clear_tool_inputs
techniques.how: With clear_tool_uses, setting clear_tool_inputs=true clears the tool call parameters as well as results once the trigger is passed; the API replaces them with placeholder text.
techniques.loses: Invalidates the cached prefix, so set clear_at_least to make the rewrite worthwhile; cleared content is unrecoverable.
techniques.paper: Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform, Anthropic; Context engineering: memory, compaction, and tool clearing (Claude cookbook)

techniques.name: DevSkills principle: persist and revise scripts (SimScrpt)
techniques.how: One developer-written principle tells the agent to persist and revise scripts instead of creating similar variants. The paper counts similar script generation as a cost-inefficient behaviour.
techniques.effect: SimScrpt in up to 68% of tasks and up to 9.57% of task cost; all 7 principles together cut cost 7.88-41.73% in 6 of 8 settings.
techniques.loses: One setting lost 1.5 pp Pass@1; the authors own the winning method.
techniques.paper: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents

methodology: Replay sampled traffic with the treatment, then a paired run per harness. Metric: billed cost per success, output tokens per task, Pass@1. For diff formats also track failed-edit rate, since a failed diff costs a retry.
gaps: Corpus has no measured share for plan-sized tool arguments beyond 1.4% of billed cost (C:024). No Codex or Kiro setting that limits argument size.

name: Agent startup cost
why: Each subagent starts by loading CLAUDE.md, git status, skills and a roster, paying that fixed cost per spawn.
detect_api: First request of a derived helper conversation: system-prompt and tool-block token count, repeated across spawns.
detect_cli: SubagentStart hook plus first-turn input tokens in the sidechain transcript.
fix_api: Identical prefix across helpers with cache_control breakpoints so startup is cache-read priced.
fix_cli: omitClaudeMd for helpers, skip skill preloads, use Explore/Plan agent types, keep description tokens under the 15k warning.

techniques.name: Subagent startup context contents
techniques.how: Helper loads CLAUDE.md, git status, preloaded skills, sibling roster and tool descriptions; description tokens above 15k warn.
techniques.effect: Size not measured per helper in corpus.
techniques.loses: Dropping CLAUDE.md loses project rules.
techniques.paper: Claude Code subagents documentation

techniques.name: Stable per-type prefix
techniques.how: Keep one fixed prefix per agent type and put dynamic content after it.
techniques.effect: -1.0% stable prefix; -7.6% dynamic content after prefix (C:052).
techniques.loses: Blanket 1h TTL is +8.6% worse.
techniques.paper: C:052 prompt cache analysis

techniques.name: Prompt caching with cache_control
techniques.how: Mark the static prefix as cacheable so repeat spawns read it.
techniques.loses: Prefix change invalidates cache.
techniques.paper: A:199 prompt caching documentation

methodology: Measure first-turn tokens before and after omitting each startup item; check helper task success.
gaps: No per-helper startup size measurement in corpus.

name: Model switch rewrote the cache
why: Each model has its own cache, so a mid-session model change rewrites the whole prefix on the next request.
detect_api: Rewrite where the model field differs from the previous call on the same key (cascade step 2 after compaction).
detect_cli: Model per call in the transcript; PreModelSwitch hook events; /model events.
fix_api: No corpus source for a gateway guard; DevX proposal: sticky model per conversation key with a switch guard that warns when the cache is warm. Class 2.
fix_cli: Pick model and effort at session start; use a PreModelSwitch hook to confirm; avoid opusplan toggles and skills whose frontmatter names a model.

techniques.name: PreModelSwitch hook and model confirmation
techniques.how: A hook can require or skip confirmation; /model confirms only while the cache is warm.
techniques.loses: Confirms but does not block intended routing.
techniques.paper: Claude Code docs, How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Cache diagnostics reason model_changed
techniques.how: Providers report why a miss happened (model_changed, tools_changed, reasoning_effort_changed and others) against a baseline response id.
techniques.loses: OpenAI GPT-5.6+ only.
techniques.paper: OpenAI, Prompt cache diagnostics

techniques.name: DevX proposal: sticky model plus switch guard
techniques.how: Gateway pins model per conversation key and routes only at session boundaries. No corpus source.
techniques.loses: Blocks cheap-model downgrades mid-task.
techniques.paper: DevX proposal (C:055 supplies the invalidation facts)

methodology: Compare CPS with and without a pinned model on paired tasks; count rewrites caused by switches.
gaps: No corpus source for a gateway-side guard.

name: Old replies replayed
why: The model's earlier prose answers are re-read on every later call though rarely needed.
detect_api: Gateway: sum of text blocks in earlier assistant messages, times later cache-read price (hermes A6).
detect_cli: gateway signal only.
fix_api: Compaction (compact_20260112) rewrites dialogue; masking does NOT touch assistant text. Treat as low priority: history is small in billed cost.
fix_cli: Compact Instructions in CLAUDE.md or /compact focus so the summary keeps decisions and drops narration; Codex experimental_compact_prompt_file.

techniques.name: Server-side compaction (compact_20260112)
techniques.how: Beta context edit that fires at `trigger` (default 150K, minimum 50K), summarises the conversation into a typed compaction block, accepts custom `instructions` and `pause_after_compaction`.
techniques.effect: Cookbook: peak 335,279 to 169,164 tokens with a 2,783-token summary; high-level facts kept 3/3, obscure specifics 0/3. Single run. Figures are from A:271.
techniques.loses: Loses verbatim detail; next turn rebuilds the cache; on short sessions the summary call costs more than it saves.
techniques.paper: Context engineering: memory, compaction, and tool clearing (Claude cookbook)

techniques.name: LLM-Summary condenser
techniques.how: Every N turns an LLM summarises older turns into one block, keeping the last M verbatim (N=21, M=10 in the study).
techniques.effect: Qwen3-Coder solve rate 53.8% vs 53.4% raw; summary cost up to 7.2% of instance; runs lengthen (52 vs 44 turns).
techniques.loses: Costs more than masking; trajectory elongation.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains Research); Memory Condensation Strategies (arXiv)

techniques.name: LLMLingua-2 token-classification compression
techniques.how: A trained classifier keeps or drops each token of the prompt, with no LLM generation step.
techniques.effect: Abstract: 3x-6x faster than prior compressors, 1.6x-2.9x end-to-end latency gain at 2x-5x compression. Cost saving not measured on agents.
techniques.loses: Compressors saved nothing or lost in the one large agent study; keep off by default (C:024).
techniques.paper: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression (Tsinghua/Microsoft)

methodology: Paired replay: raw vs compaction with a recall probe of decisions made in earlier assistant turns; cost per successful task.
gaps: No corpus measurement isolates assistant-text replay; C:024 puts all history under 1% of billed cost.

name: Clarification loops
why: Each question the agent asks adds a turn and re-sends the context.
detect_api: Assistant turns ending in a question with no tool call, followed by a short user reply.
detect_cli: Transcript turns with no tool call ending in a question mark; Notification or elicitation events.
fix_api: Add persistence prompt text via system prompt injection at the gateway (class 2).
fix_cli: Bias-to-action prompts, plan mode, interview-then-SPEC.md pattern.

techniques.name: Persistence / bias-to-action prompting
techniques.how: Tell the agent to proceed and not ask unless blocked; give stop conditions.
techniques.effect: Cost of asking not measured in corpus.
techniques.loses: Wrong assumptions on ambiguous tasks.
techniques.paper: Model prompting guides

techniques.name: Plan mode
techniques.how: Plan first, approve once, then execute.
techniques.loses: Extra planning turn.
techniques.paper: Claude Code docs; A:053

techniques.name: Interview-then-SPEC.md
techniques.how: One structured interview writes a spec, then a fresh session executes.
techniques.loses: Upfront cost.
techniques.paper: Claude Code best practices

methodology: A/B bias-to-action prompt versus control on matched tasks: clarification count, cost, success.
gaps: Cost of clarification is not measured.

name: Screenshot accumulation
why: Every screenshot stays in context and is re-billed each turn until compaction, so old images keep costing input tokens.
detect_api: Count image blocks in request messages per call; estimate tokens as w*h/750 (hermes formula); flag images older than N turns still carried.
detect_cli: Transcript scan for image blocks in tool_result entries; PostToolUse hook counts screenshots per session and their age in turns.
fix_api: Class 0 alert first. Then, after a paired CPS win, mask images older than M turns with a placeholder (observation masking). DevX proposal: downscale before forwarding (no corpus source).
fix_cli: Rely on Claude Code's oldest-image eviction past its cap; DevX proposal: a PostToolUse hook that downsizes screenshots. Context editing clear_tool_uses can clear old tool results.

techniques.name: Observation masking
techniques.how: Rolling window of M=10 turns keeps recent observations and replaces older ones with a placeholder.
techniques.effect: About half the cost of the raw agent at a solve rate matching LLM-Summary (SWE-bench Verified, SWE-agent).
techniques.loses: Tuned per agent (M=58 for OpenHands); paper tests text observations, so images are an extrapolation.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains, arXiv 2508.21433)

techniques.name: Claude Code oldest-image eviction
techniques.how: When the next request would pass the image or PDF cap, Claude Code removes a batch of the oldest images and PDFs.
techniques.effect: Costs one slower turn per batch while the cache reprocesses from the earliest changed message.
techniques.loses: Claude can no longer see removed images.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Context editing: clear_tool_uses_20250919
techniques.how: Clears old tool results past a trigger (example 30000 input tokens), keeps the last N tool uses, and clear_at_least ensures each clear is worth the cache write.
techniques.loses: Clearing invalidates the cache prefix; extracts do not say whether images are cleared.
techniques.paper: Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform

methodology: Paired A/B on the same tasks: baseline vs masking or downscale, metric cost per successful task, check task success does not drop before enabling.
gaps: no corpus source for image downscale or the w*h/750 formula. DevX proposal: Pillow downscale to a max edge before forwarding. Corpus does not confirm context editing clears images.

name: Visual iteration loops
why: Each edit-then-screenshot cycle adds a fresh image and a model turn, so a long loop multiplies image tokens.
detect_api: Per session, count edit-tool-call then image-bearing tool-result cycles; flag more than 3 per task.
detect_cli: Transcript or hook sequence: Edit/Write followed by a screenshot tool result; count cycles per prompt.
fix_api: Class 0 alert, then mask old screenshots after each cycle (observation masking). DevX proposal: cap cycles at N and force a text summary.
fix_cli: Eviction of oldest images (Claude Code) bounds the cost; DevX proposal: a hook that warns on the 4th cycle. Lower effort for subagents doing the loop (A:282).

techniques.name: Observation masking
techniques.how: Keep the last M=10 turns of observations and mask the rest, so each loop iteration drops the prior screenshot.
techniques.effect: About half the cost of the raw agent, matching LLM-Summary solve rate (SWE-bench Verified).
techniques.loses: Masking loses at 7 events or fewer (C:133 as noted); text-only evidence.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains, arXiv 2508.21433)

techniques.name: Claude Code oldest-image eviction
techniques.how: Removes a batch of the oldest images when the cap is near.
techniques.loses: Earlier screenshots become invisible to the model.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Effort parameter
techniques.how: output_config.effort low to max changes tool-call count and verbosity; lower effort gives fewer tool calls.
techniques.effect: not measured in corpus for visual loops
techniques.loses: Behavioural signal, not a budget; run a sweep on your own evals.
techniques.paper: Effort parameter (Claude)

methodology: Replay recorded UI tasks with and without the cycle cap; compare success rate and cost per successful task.
gaps: no corpus source for a visual-loop cap or the 3-cycle threshold. DevX proposal: threshold calibrated per task type.

name: Cache not reused
why: Writes never read back, missing caching, or a prefix below the minimum cacheable length mean the premium or full price is paid for nothing.
detect_api: cw never followed by cr (A35); uncached input above 10k (A21); prefix below minimum with both cache fields 0 (A24).
detect_cli: Same usage fields; headers show a gateway stripping cache_control if cw is always 0.
fix_api: Inject cache_control at the system message or second-to-last user turn; lengthen sub-minimum prompts. Class 0, then 2.
fix_cli: Ensure gateways forward cache_control and the anthropic-beta header; read /usage hit ratio and the likely cause.

techniques.name: cache_control_injection_points
techniques.how: LiteLLM injects the cache marker at the system message or second-to-last user turn without client edits.
techniques.effect: Cache hit costs about 10% of fresh input.
techniques.loses: Needs a LiteLLM proxy; vendor blog.
techniques.paper: LiteLLM, 5 ways to cut Claude Code costs with LiteLLM

techniques.name: Automatic caching and minimum-length rules
techniques.how: Top-level cache_control caches automatically; below the model minimum both cache fields are 0 with no error.
techniques.effect: Minimums 512 to 4,096 tokens depending on model.
techniques.loses: Silent failure; verify with usage fields.
techniques.paper: Claude prompt caching docs; Start Debugging, Add Prompt Caching to an Anthropic SDK App

techniques.name: Prompt lengthening to cross the threshold
techniques.how: Extend a 900-token prompt to 1100 tokens so it can hit.
techniques.loses: OpenAI case; extra tokens cost if hit rate stays low.
techniques.paper: OpenAI, Prompt Caching 201

methodology: Hit-rate wrapper from usage fields (C:051), then paired CPS A/B with injection on.
gaps: Gateway stripping cache_control is documented only in C:055; no measured prevalence.

name: Correction churn
why: A correction adds turns and a wrong attempt stays in context.
detect_api: Correction regex on user turns; no corpus source for the regex. DevX proposal.
detect_cli: Same correction matcher over transcript user turns; /rewind use.
fix_api: Alert only (class 0).
fix_cli: Specific first prompt; /clear after two failed corrections; repeated corrections into CLAUDE.md; /rewind.

techniques.name: Two-failed-corrections then /clear
techniques.how: After two failed fixes, clear context and restart with a better prompt.
techniques.loses: Loses context.
techniques.paper: Claude Code best practices

techniques.name: /rewind restore
techniques.how: Roll back to before the wrong attempt.
techniques.loses: Discards work.
techniques.paper: Claude Code checkpointing

techniques.name: TokenEconomizer micro-skills
techniques.how: Short skills that encode repeated fixes.
techniques.loses: Benchmark only.
techniques.paper: TokenEconomizer

techniques.name: DevSkills
techniques.how: Reusable guidance from past corrections.
techniques.loses: Benchmark only.

methodology: Track correction rate before and after CLAUDE.md additions.
gaps: CORRECTION_RE text is not in the corpus.

name: Agents racing the cache
why: Parallel helpers that start within seconds each write the same prefix because the cache entry exists only after the first response starts.
detect_api: Calls with the same prefix hash within 10s, both cw above 5k.
detect_cli: Subagent start timestamps and first-call usage per session_id.
fix_api: DevX proposal: single-flight lock; the first request goes alone, the rest wait for its first response. No corpus source for the lock itself. Class 2.
fix_cli: Prefer forks; workflow fan-out already holds all but the first agent up to 5s.

techniques.name: Wait for first response before parallel requests
techniques.how: The entry becomes available only after the first response begins; send the rest after.
techniques.loses: Adds latency to the fan-out.
techniques.paper: Claude prompt caching docs

techniques.name: Workflow fan-out hold
techniques.how: Holds all but the first agent up to 5s so they read its cache.
techniques.loses: Beyond 5s the race returns.
techniques.paper: Claude Code docs, How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Batch caching: 1h block plus one shared-prefix request first
techniques.how: Best effort; send one shared-prefix request first, using a 1h block.
techniques.loses: Best effort only.
techniques.paper: Claude prompt caching docs

methodology: Measure duplicate cw tokens before and after a hold on a fan-out workload.
gaps: No corpus source for a gateway lock; labelled DevX proposal.

name: Too much tool output
why: One large Read, MCP or fetch result enters history and is paid again at cache-read price on every later call until compaction.
detect_api: Tool_result block tokens in the next request body for non-Bash tools; flag above 4,000, charge tokens minus 2,000 (hermes BIG_RESULT/BIG_KEEP, unvalidated).
detect_cli: Gateway signal only for size; PostToolUse hook gives tool_response and OTel tool_result gives tool_name and duration (C:002).
fix_api: Cap and paginate in the tool server (25,000 token default is Anthropic's own), and set clear_tool_uses with a trigger, keep, clear_at_least and exclude_tools. Gateway truncation of tool_result is a DevX proposal and must be applied identically every turn to keep the prefix stable.
fix_cli: Codex: tool_output_token_limit (default 12,000; 8,000 and 6,000 in examples). Claude Code: PostToolUse updatedToolOutput hook to cap results; never truncate tracebacks or edit anchors. Observation masking only above about 10 events.

techniques.name: Tool-response pagination, range selection, filtering, truncation
techniques.how: Anthropic's tool-writing guide advises combining pagination, range selection, filtering and truncation with sensible defaults, and steering the agent with the truncation message. Claude Code caps tool responses at 25,000 tokens.
techniques.effect: Concise vs detailed Slack response: 72 vs 206 tokens in the guide's example.
techniques.loses: Truncation can cut needed content; the guide says to give helpful steering text.
techniques.paper: Writing effective tools for AI agents, Anthropic

techniques.name: Observation masking (rolling window M)
techniques.how: Replace tool observations older than the last M turns with a placeholder, keeping all reasoning and actions: o'_i = p_i if i < t - M, else o_i.
techniques.effect: M=10 cut Gemini 2.5 Flash cost $0.41 to $0.18 (-56.1%); Qwen3-Coder solve rate 54.8% vs 53.4% raw; DiscoveryBench: +8.6% token saving, only method that saved.
techniques.loses: At 7 events or fewer it lost 45% to 149%; window needs tuning per scaffold; SWE-agent only.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap: Observation Masking vs LLM Summarization (JetBrains Research); Evaluating Memory Condensation Strategies for Coding Agents in Data-Driven Scientific Discovery

techniques.name: Server-side tool-result clearing (clear_tool_uses_20250919)
techniques.how: When input tokens pass a trigger (default 100,000; docs example 30,000) the API clears the oldest tool results, keeps the last N (default 3), and honours clear_at_least and exclude_tools.
techniques.effect: Cookbook, one synthetic task: peak context 335,279 (file reads 96.3%) down to 173,137, no dollars measured.
techniques.loses: Clearing invalidates the cached prefix; single run; reads not re-fetched are lost.
techniques.paper: Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform; Context engineering cookbook, Anthropic

techniques.name: Codex tool_output_token_limit
techniques.how: Config key setting the token budget for storing each tool output in history; default 12,000.
techniques.loses: Smaller cap means less is kept and large files get re-read after compaction (issue 16812 pattern).
techniques.paper: Codex configuration reference, OpenAI; Mastering Context Compaction in Codex CLI (Vaughan blog)

methodology: Sweep the cap at 6k, 12k and 25k on replayed traffic; metric billed cost per success, re-read count and turn of first edit (C:024 design: paired, provider-billed, cache reset between arms). For masking sweep M at 5, 10, 20 per scaffold.
gaps: No corpus measurement of billed saving from a size cap. Corpus holds no Kiro setting. LLMLingua on agent tool output is untested in corpus (A:079 covers prose prompts).

name: Noisy and repeated terminal output
why: Build, install, test and lint output is mostly passing lines and repeats, but it sits in history and is re-billed every turn.
detect_api: Bash tool_result above 4,000 tokens; duplicate-line share above 0.5 on 20+ normalised lines; repeated traceback key (md5 of last 5 normalised lines) or repeated linter result hash (hermes A87, A82, A84).
detect_cli: Gateway signal only; PostToolUse hook receives the command and output; Aider /tokens shows the context breakdown (C:127).
fix_api: Gateway cannot rewrite a command. Use clear_tool_uses for old results, a tool-server cap, or a subagent for noisy commands. Output compressors stay off by default.
fix_cli: Claude Code PreToolUse hook that rewrites test commands to pipe through grep for FAIL/ERROR with head -100 (updatedInput). Delegate verbose runs to a subagent. Codex tool_output_token_limit. Never pipe compressed output into shell counting.

techniques.name: PreToolUse hook rewriting the command (updatedInput)
techniques.how: Hook inspects tool_input.command for npm test, pytest or go test and returns an updated command piped through grep -A 5 for FAIL/ERROR/error: and head -100. The doc also describes a hook that greps ERROR from a 10,000-line log.
techniques.effect: Doc says tens of thousands of tokens down to hundreds; no measurement.
techniques.loses: Can drop critical lines: a pytest rule had 56.1% marker recall at 31.9% saving before a fix; only one hook may rewrite the same input.
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code); Automate actions with hooks (guide), Anthropic; Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction

techniques.name: RTK deterministic CLI proxy and Headroom API proxy (measured, off by default)
techniques.how: RTK is a PreToolUse hook that routes shell commands through a CLI proxy with strategy-based compression; Headroom sits at ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and optimises payloads in flight.
techniques.effect: RTK -2.7% billed cost (not significant); RTK-ML cut 38.4% of tool-output tokens but cost +6.8%; Headroom +48.4%; Codex Headroom -12.49%.
techniques.loses: Sign flips by harness; compression delayed the first edit and raised repeated searches; compressed grep fed to a shell pipeline gave silently wrong counts.
techniques.paper: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction (Weinberger and Hozez, PointFive); TokenEconomizer (Li et al., UC Berkeley and Microsoft Research)

techniques.name: Preservation-first filter rules with marker recall gate
techniques.how: Score a filter by savings and by the share of task-critical marker lines kept. The pytest rule was changed to preserve traceback lines.
techniques.effect: Original rule 31.9% savings at 56.1% recall; fixed rule 15.3% savings at 99.2% recall, 24 pytest observations.
techniques.loses: Halves the nominal saving; interactive task success was not run.
techniques.paper: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction

techniques.name: Delegate verbose operations to subagents
techniques.how: Running tests or reading logs in a subagent keeps the verbose output in its context and returns a summary to the main thread.
techniques.loses: The subagent's own requests still bill; no shared cache with parent.
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code); How Claude Code uses prompt caching

methodology: Per C:024: paired runs, billed cost per successful task, cache reset between arms, plus 99% marker recall on a labelled set of failing logs before any filter goes live. Prove the hook is active (byte-diff output) before reading results.
gaps: No corpus source for build or install output (xcodebuild, npm install) filtering. Vendor 75-80% claims for git/ls/grep are unmeasured (C:024).

name: Repeated tasks across sessions
why: The same request is solved again from scratch in a later session of the project, paying the whole exploration again.
detect_api: Gateway: first user message of a conversation key with word overlap 60%+ against an earlier conversation of the same caller/project (hermes #15), flagged as spend-to-review.
detect_cli: UserPromptSubmit hook first prompt per session (C:074) with project id; same overlap rule.
fix_api: Class 0 alert only. A semantic response cache (Portkey simple/semantic cache) is a Class 2 candidate but unproven for multi-turn agent tasks, so it stays off.
fix_cli: Turn recurring tasks into a skill or CLAUDE.md note, or let auto memory save them; TokenEconomizer-style micro-skills are the closest measured method.

techniques.name: TokenEconomizer experience-grounded micro-skills
techniques.how: External controller condenses past trajectories into digests, an LLM proposes micro-skills with regex detectors, activates one only after confirmation on several tasks with non-overlapping edited files and a need-rate threshold, retires it when a trace contradicts it.
techniques.effect: Token cost down 18.4-30.9% across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI with comparable pass@1 (within 3 points); cumulative savings positive by task six.
techniques.loses: Costs more on early tasks; micro-skills go stale; tasks were independent SWE-Bench issues.
techniques.paper: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents (TokenEconomizer; Berkeley/Microsoft)

techniques.name: Semantic cache (Portkey simple and semantic modes)
techniques.how: Gateway returns a stored response when a new request's embedding matches a cached one; simple mode needs an exact match.
techniques.effect: not measured for agent tasks in corpus
techniques.loses: Wrong-answer risk when the repo changed; targets repetitive single-turn chat.
techniques.paper: Simple and semantic cache (Portkey); GPT Semantic Cache; MeanCache

techniques.name: Auto memory / CLAUDE.md
techniques.how: Persist solved procedures as notes that load next session.
techniques.effect: Memory run: session 2 peak 172,623 vs 333,977 tokens without memory (4 of 8 documents re-read).
techniques.loses: Single synthetic run.
techniques.paper: How Claude remembers your project; Context engineering cookbook

methodology: Cross-session sequence test as in C:028: ordered task stream per repo, cumulative cost vs default, pass@1 within 3 points, report break-even task index.
gaps: No corpus technique detects 'same task' beyond word overlap; semantic caching evidence is single-turn only.

name: Failed, retried and polling calls
why: Repeated failing attempts keep re-sending growing context with no progress.
detect_api: Repeated near-identical tool-error results and requests in one derived conversation.
detect_cli: Failure-signature normalization over transcript tool errors; repeat count.
fix_api: Rate-based circuit breaker and loop guard at gateway.
fix_cli: Percentile turn budget, redirect then abort; maxTurns; fix error messages; constrained decoding for schema failures.

techniques.name: TokenEconomizer failure-loop guard
techniques.how: Normalize failure signatures, set turn budget Bi = beta times Q_p, rule trigger then LLM judge, redirect then abort; forced stop at kappa=2.5.
techniques.effect: 17% of tasks and 32% of spend failed; 51% of spend after first repetition; guard alone gives single-digit savings.
techniques.loses: 36 of 50 successful runs also repeat a signature.
techniques.paper: TokenEconomizer

techniques.name: Turn-control (fixed p75, dynamic limits)
techniques.how: Cap turns at a percentile, then grow dynamically p25 to p50.
techniques.loses: Capability wall on hard tasks.
techniques.paper: Turn-control study

techniques.name: Rate-based circuit breaker
techniques.how: Trip when error rate exceeds a threshold.
techniques.loses: False trips.

techniques.name: Actionable tool errors and constrained decoding
techniques.how: Clear error messages; constrained decoding for schema-invalid output.
techniques.loses: Summaries mask failure signals (C:130).
techniques.paper: Tool design guide; constrained decoding papers; A:059 ReTest

methodology: Replay logged failure loops with guard on; measure saved spend and tasks wrongly stopped.
gaps: Polling-loop specific technique has no source beyond the generic breaker and A:059 ReTest.

name: Repeated screenshots
why: Identical or back-to-back screenshots pay image tokens again for no new information.
detect_api: Hash image bytes per request (md5 repeat, A114/A112); flag a retake after a failed browser call (A120).
detect_cli: Transcript: consecutive screenshot tool calls, identical image hash, retake after a tool error.
fix_api: Class 0 alert. DevX proposal: perceptual-hash dedup returning the earlier image reference (no corpus source); mask older copies (observation masking).
fix_cli: Oldest-image eviction (Claude Code); DevX proposal: a PreToolUse hook that blocks a screenshot repeated with no intervening edit.

techniques.name: Observation masking
techniques.how: Replace observations outside a 10-turn window with a placeholder.
techniques.effect: About half the cost of the raw agent at matched solve rate (SWE-bench Verified).
techniques.loses: Text observations only in the paper.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains, arXiv 2508.21433)

techniques.name: Claude Code oldest-image eviction
techniques.how: Drops oldest images and PDFs past the cap.
techniques.loses: Removed images cannot be seen.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Image input pricing
techniques.how: 1 input image token is billed as 1 token and a cached image token at 0.1, so a repeat under a cache costs less than a fresh one.
techniques.loses: Needs a warm cache.
techniques.paper: Vertex Provisioned Throughput

methodology: Count duplicate hashes on a week of traffic, estimate savings as repeats times image tokens, then A/B the dedup on a sample.
gaps: no corpus source for perceptual-hash dedup. DevX proposal only.

name: Progress narration
why: Text beside tool calls ('now I will...') adds output tokens that cost the highest rate and carry no result.
detect_api: Assistant text over 50 tokens in a response that also has a tool_use block (A54).
detect_cli: Transcript: assistant text blocks over 50 tokens adjacent to tool calls.
fix_api: Class 1/2: set text.verbosity or response style default, and drop preamble prompting. Cap with max_tokens as a ceiling (guard, not a fix).
fix_cli: Output styles (outputStyle setting) or prompt text to remove preambles; Codex advice is to remove preamble prompting. Lower effort gives terser tool calls.

techniques.name: text.verbosity
techniques.how: Sets default detail low, medium or high; task-specific length goes in the prompt.
techniques.loses: Broad brevity prompts can make answers too short.
techniques.paper: GPT-5.6 guide

techniques.name: Remove tool preambles
techniques.how: Delete prompting for upfront plans and status updates; preambles are steerable in frequency.
techniques.loses: Hurts user visibility; preambles can cause early stopping when prompted.
techniques.paper: Codex prompting guide; GPT-5 prompting guide

techniques.name: Effort parameter
techniques.how: output_config.effort affects all output, including text and tool calls; lower gives fewer, terser calls.
techniques.loses: Behavioural signal, not a budget.
techniques.paper: Effort parameter (Claude)

methodology: A/B narration-off vs on; metric output tokens per task and task success.
gaps: no corpus source for a numeric saving from removing narration. Claude Opus 5 does not shorten with lower effort (A:200); prompt explicitly.

name: Whole-file reads
why: A Read with no offset or limit pulls the full file (over 5,000 tokens) into history when a slice would answer the question.
detect_api: Read tool_use with no offset and limit in input, and the following tool_result above 5,000 tokens (hermes A71); charge tokens minus 2,000.
detect_cli: Gateway signal only; PreToolUse hook sees tool_input without offset or limit.
fix_api: Alert, then Class 2 DevX proposal: return a path reference or the first N lines with a steering note for an oversized unsliced read (A:284 truncation guidance). Clearing handles file reads already in history.
fix_cli: Claude Code: Read deny rules for generated and vendored paths; LSP plugin for symbol lookup; PreToolUse hook to block oversize unsliced reads is a DevX proposal. Codex: tool_output_token_limit. After compaction Claude Code returns files over 5,000 tokens as a path reference.

techniques.name: Code intelligence plugin (go to definition) instead of reading files
techniques.how: A language server returns the definition or references directly so the agent does not read through candidate files to locate a symbol.
techniques.loses: Needs a language server per language; typed languages named in the doc.
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code); Set up Claude Code in a monorepo or large codebase, Anthropic

techniques.name: Path-reference stub for oversized files
techniques.how: Claude Code re-reads up to five recent files after compaction and returns any file over 5,000 tokens as a path reference, shown as Referenced file, without content.
techniques.loses: The agent must read again if it needs the content.
techniques.paper: Explore the context window, Anthropic

techniques.name: Tool-response range selection and truncation guidance
techniques.how: Offer pagination and range parameters with defaults on any tool that can return a large file, and word the truncation message so the agent makes small targeted reads.
techniques.effect: 72 vs 206 tokens for concise vs detailed response in the guide's example.
techniques.loses: Can hide needed content.
techniques.paper: Writing effective tools for AI agents, Anthropic

techniques.name: Large-file re-read after compaction (failure case)
techniques.how: Codex issue 16812: a 93 KB analysis, 58 KB plan and 610 KB OpenAPI spec had to be re-read after every compaction. Mitigation given: lower tool_output_token_limit and put durable facts in AGENTS.md.
techniques.loses: Smaller limit keeps less context.
techniques.paper: Mastering Context Compaction in Codex CLI (Vaughan blog)

methodology: Replay, then paired A/B on the guard: billed cost per success, extra Read calls with offset, first-edit turn (C:024 reports compression delayed first edit 0.94 turns). Count outlier reads over 5,000 tokens before and after.
gaps: No corpus source gives a read-size threshold or a measured saving for forcing slices. Hook-based read blocking is a DevX proposal.

name: Duplicate reading across agents
why: A helper re-reads files the parent already read because it does not share context.
detect_api: Same file contents appearing in multiple derived conversations under one parent.
detect_cli: Repeated Read/Grep on identical paths across sidechains in transcripts.
fix_api: No corpus source for gateway side. DevX proposal: cache identical read results across helpers.
fix_cli: Use fork when parent context is needed; ask helpers to return paths and line ranges (DevX proposal); apply DevSkills guidance.

techniques.name: DevSkills (reuse context, justify re-reads)
techniques.how: Skill instructs the agent to state a hypothesis, reuse context and justify re-reads.
techniques.effect: SubRetrv cost behaviour reduced 51.52% and 43.57% in two settings.
techniques.loses: Benchmark settings only.
techniques.paper: A:059 cost-inefficient agent behaviors (SubRetrv, SimScrpt, ReTest)

techniques.name: Fork versus fresh subagent choice
techniques.how: Fork inherits parent context so no re-read; fresh helper starts cold.
techniques.loses: Fork inherits full parent prefix cost.
techniques.paper: Claude Code subagents documentation

techniques.name: Structure-aware retrieval (CodeGraph)
techniques.how: Graph-based retrieval to avoid re-reading.
techniques.effect: Raised cost by up to 28.14% in the source.
techniques.loses: Cost increase, so not a fix.

methodology: Count repeated reads per task before and after DevSkills; check pass rate unchanged.
gaps: No gateway-side source.

name: Agent coordination chatter
why: Teammates exchange messages and idle-wake, and each message re-enters context.
detect_api: No gateway source. DevX proposal: count derived conversations that alternate with near-identical prefixes.
detect_cli: Team mailbox message count, TeammateIdle hook events, per-teammate tokens.
fix_api: No corpus source; DevX proposal only.
fix_cli: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=0; drop roster via disallowedTools on SendMessage; TeammateIdle hook.

techniques.name: Mailbox messaging (one message per recipient)
techniques.how: Teams exchange mailbox messages, one per recipient; idle teammates wake via hook.
techniques.loses: Disabling teams loses parallel collaboration.
techniques.paper: Claude Code agent teams documentation

techniques.name: Drop roster by disabling SendMessage
techniques.how: The sibling roster only appears with SendMessage; disallowedTools removes it.
techniques.loses: No peer messaging.
techniques.paper: Claude Code subagents documentation

techniques.name: Delegation floor cost and brief granularity
techniques.how: Each delegation has a fixed cost; brief granularity has an optimum.
techniques.effect: 84-98% at worker rate for orchestrator case.
techniques.loses: Too fine briefs net negative.
techniques.paper: C:012 orchestrator analysis

methodology: A/B teams on versus off on matched multi-part tasks; compare cost per resolved task.
gaps: No API-side source.

name: Large images and PDFs
why: One large image or PDF can cost thousands of input tokens in a single call, then keeps being re-sent.
detect_api: Image over 1,200 tokens (A111), cost (itok-800) times input price; PDF read (A115); same document as page images and text (A116/A117).
detect_cli: Transcript: Read of a PDF or large image, tool result token size, same file read twice in different forms.
fix_api: Class 0 alert, then DevX proposal: downscale oversized images and extract PDF text first (no corpus source). Clear after use via clear_tool_uses.
fix_cli: Prefer pdftotext or OCR text (named in hermes); Claude Code evicts oldest images/PDFs past its cap. DevX proposal: a hook that downsizes images on Read.

techniques.name: Context editing: clear_tool_uses_20250919
techniques.how: Clears large tool results after a trigger, with exclude_tools and clear_at_least to protect the cache.
techniques.loses: Clearing breaks the cache prefix; extracts do not say it clears images.
techniques.paper: Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform

techniques.name: Claude Code image/PDF eviction
techniques.how: Removes a batch of oldest images and PDFs when caps would be exceeded.
techniques.loses: Model loses sight of removed documents.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Observation masking
techniques.how: Rolling window of recent observations, placeholder for the rest.
techniques.effect: About half cost at matched solve rate (text tasks).
techniques.loses: Extrapolation to PDFs.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains, arXiv 2508.21433)

methodology: Compare answer quality on a document QA set for image vs extracted-text input; gate on equal accuracy.
gaps: no corpus source for image downscale, pdftotext or ocrmypdf choice. DevX proposal; hermes names pdftotext and ocrmypdf.

name: Broad or unbounded searches
why: A grep or find with no path, glob or type limit returns hundreds of matches that stay in history and push the agent to read more.
detect_api: Grep/Glob tool_use with no path, glob or type input, or Bash grep/rg/find; result above 100 lines or 1,000 tokens (hermes A73, A79).
detect_cli: Gateway signal only; PostToolUse hook gets tool_input and the result.
fix_api: Alert. DevX proposal: cap search tool results in the tool server and return a steering message to narrow the query (A:284). Clearing for old results.
fix_cli: Claude Code: language-server plugin for symbol lookup; built-in searches already respect .gitignore; Read deny rules also drop denied paths from Grep and Glob (best effort). Hook to cap output. Aider: repo map with --map-tokens.

techniques.name: Structural retrieval with ast-grep hybrid (RTK-ML)
techniques.how: Query-aware ranking and ast-grep structural matches replace raw ripgrep output, grouping and ranking hits under a token budget.
techniques.effect: ripgrep 310.9 matches, 2,905 tokens, 0.66 precision vs hybrid 170.9, 2,090 tokens, 0.995 precision (8 tasks, 38 queries); retrieval-quality proxy only.
techniques.loses: Whole RTK-ML arm raised billed cost 6.8%; no task success recorded for this test.
techniques.paper: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction

techniques.name: Code intelligence (LSP) navigation
techniques.how: Go-to-definition replaces a grep followed by reading several candidate files.
techniques.loses: Typed languages; binary per machine.
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code); Set up Claude Code in a monorepo, Anthropic

techniques.name: DevSkills: state a hypothesis before retrieval, justify re-reads
techniques.how: Principles written by developers tell the agent to state a concrete hypothesis before retrieving, reuse available context and justify necessary re-reads; addresses subsumed retrieval.
techniques.effect: Subsumed retrieval in 64.33-92.33% of tasks and 5.01-11.41% of cost; SubRetrv fell 51.52% and 43.57% in one config.
techniques.loses: One setting lost 1.5 pp Pass@1; a structure-aware retrieval tool raised cost up to 28.14%.
techniques.paper: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents

techniques.name: Aider repo map with --map-tokens
techniques.how: Graph-ranked tree-sitter symbol map under a token budget (default 1k) lets the model find files without searching; 0 disables it.
techniques.loses: Budget is soft; map grows when no files are added.
techniques.paper: How to Manage the Aider Context Window and Token Budgets; How to Reduce Aider Token Usage

methodology: Paired run with the search cap or LSP on: billed cost per success, repeated-search count and match precision against test-grounded gold (C:024 method). Check that no compressed search output feeds a shell pipeline.
gaps: No corpus source on the right result-line cap; the 100-line threshold is hermes's, unvalidated.

name: Bloated JSON and query results
why: Large JSON or DB results carry many unused fields, IDs and serialisation wrappers, and the whole payload is re-billed every turn.
detect_api: tool_result text that parses as JSON above a size line; unused-field share needs a later-use check, so alert only (hermes A98-A100, thresholds not given).
detect_cli: Gateway signal only; MCP tool names visible via OTel with OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 (C:002).
fix_api: Fix at the tool or MCP server: return high-signal fields and add a response_format enum (concise/detailed). Gateway-side field projection is a DevX proposal, needs per-tool schema and a recall test.
fix_cli: Codex tool_output_token_limit and enabled_tools filtering; Claude Code PostToolUse updatedToolOutput hook to project fields with jq (DevX proposal). Prefer CLI tools such as gh over MCP servers per the doc.

techniques.name: response_format enum (concise vs detailed) and high-signal fields
techniques.how: Tools return names and content, not uuid, mime_type or 256px_image_url, and expose a ResponseFormat enum so the agent picks concise or detailed. The guide likens extra formats to GraphQL field choice.
techniques.effect: Concise 72 tokens vs detailed 206 tokens, about one third, one Slack example.
techniques.loses: Agent may need IDs for follow-up calls; best format varies by task and model, test it.
techniques.paper: Writing effective tools for AI agents, Anthropic

techniques.name: Tool-result clearing for re-fetchable payloads
techniques.how: clear_tool_uses removes old API and file results the agent can fetch again.
techniques.effect: Cookbook peak 335,279 to 173,137 tokens, single synthetic run. Figures are from A:271.
techniques.loses: Cache rewrite per clear; not for results that cannot be re-fetched (use exclude_tools).
techniques.paper: Context engineering cookbook; Context editing on the Claude Developer Platform, Anthropic

techniques.name: LLMLingua coarse-to-fine prompt compression (untested on JSON)
