techniques.how: A budget controller allocates compression per segment, then token-level iterative compression drops low-information tokens using a small LM's perplexity.
techniques.effect: GSM8K 2,366 to 117 tokens at 77.33 EM vs 78.85 (about 20x).
techniques.loses: Tested on prose prompts; byte-exact JSON and agent traces are not in the corpus; C:024 saw compression break exactness.
techniques.paper: LLMLingua (Jiang et al., Microsoft Research); LLMLingua-2 (Pan et al., Microsoft Research); Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction

methodology: For each MCP tool with large JSON: A/B concise vs detailed format on replayed tasks; metric billed cost per success and tool-selection and retrieval accuracy (the guide asks you to test response structure per task).
gaps: No corpus source for JSON minification, TOON-style formats or SQL column pruning. Field projection at a gateway is a DevX proposal.

name: Wordy and repeated output
why: Whole-file rewrites, echoed questions, repeated paragraphs and reprinted code inflate output tokens.
detect_api: Write of a file already read; question echo (A52 Jaccard 0.7); repeated paragraph 300+ chars (A53); reprinted code 300+ chars (A58); stop_reason max_tokens (A60).
detect_cli: Transcript: whole-file Write after Read of the same file, repeated text blocks, reprinted code blocks.
fix_api: Class 1: set max_tokens on every call (C:073 guard) and track stop_reason; class 2: verbosity default and concise response_format.
fix_cli: Prefer edit-style tools over whole-file Write; output style setting for concise replies. Claude Code caps tool responses at 25,000 tokens.

techniques.name: Constrained-CoT (CCoT)
techniques.how: Prompt asks for concise output; conciseness metrics measure redundancy and information flow.
techniques.loses: Over-brevity can hurt accuracy.
techniques.paper: Constrained-CoT

techniques.name: text.verbosity
techniques.how: Default level of detail low, medium or high, set per request.
techniques.loses: Can be too brief.
techniques.paper: GPT-5.6 guide

techniques.name: response_format concise
techniques.how: Enum letting the tool return concise vs detailed output.
techniques.effect: 72 vs 206 tokens in the Slack example
techniques.loses: Extra call if detail needed.
techniques.paper: Writing effective tools for AI agents

techniques.name: max_tokens ceiling
techniques.how: A hard cap on output length.
techniques.effect: maxOutputTokens=300 did not cut thinking on easy tasks and broke 7 of 25 hard ones.
techniques.loses: Truncation; a ceiling, not a reducer.
techniques.paper: Cost per task (Google blog)

methodology: Compare output tokens and edit success with whole-file vs diff edits on the same tasks.
gaps: no corpus source opened for diff-vs-whole-file edit format savings or shingle echo detection. DevX proposal: edit-format switch tested by paired CPS.

name: Web pages and search results
why: Fetched pages and search results are long, overlap each other, and are refetched, so the same text is billed repeatedly.
detect_api: Page over 4,000 tokens (A101); more than 10 distinct URLs (A103); 8-word-shingle overlap 0.5+ (A104); same URL refetched (A105); overlapping chunks (A107); refetch after compaction (A110).
detect_cli: Transcript: WebFetch/WebSearch tool results by size and URL repeat; hook counts distinct URLs per session.
fix_api: Class 0 alert; class 2 after a test: query-aware pruning of results (Provence, LongLLMLingua), cap web_search with max_uses, paginate and filter tool output. Response cache is a DevX proposal with correctness risk.
fix_cli: Claude Code caps tool responses at 25,000 tokens; design MCP tools with pagination and a concise response_format. Subagent for fetches keeps pages out of the main context.

techniques.name: Provence
techniques.how: Context pruning as sequence labelling, unified with reranking, so irrelevant sentences are dropped.
techniques.effect: Negligible to no performance drop; 49% compression noted at one point.
techniques.loses: Needs a trained pruner.
techniques.paper: Provence (arXiv 2501.16214)

techniques.name: LongLLMLingua
techniques.how: Query-aware prompt compression for long contexts.
techniques.effect: +21.4% on NaturalQuestions with about 4x fewer tokens (GPT-3.5-Turbo); 94.0% cost cut on LooGLE.
techniques.loses: Compression can drop needed facts.
techniques.paper: LongLLMLingua (arXiv 2310.06839)

techniques.name: Self-Route
techniques.how: Model self-reflection routes each query to RAG or long context.
techniques.effect: Cost down 65% on Gemini-1.5-Pro and 39% on GPT-4o at comparable quality.
techniques.loses: Pure RAG is worse than long context.
techniques.paper: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs?

techniques.name: Tool-response design
techniques.how: Pagination, filtering, truncation and a response_format enum; concise 72 tokens vs detailed 206 in the Slack example.
techniques.loses: Model may need a second call.
techniques.paper: Writing effective tools for AI agents

methodology: Paired replay of research tasks with pruned vs full pages; metric answer accuracy and cost per successful task.
gaps: no corpus source for 8-word-shingle dedup or ETag refetch skipping. Semantic caching exists in corpus (A:240 Portkey, A:113) but correctness is unproven; DevX proposal.

name: Copied history
why: Background text, chat transcripts and forked conversations are pasted or duplicated, so the same tokens enter context twice.
detect_api: Gateway: 400+ char paragraphs whose whitespace-normalised hash was seen in an earlier prompt of the project (A7); prompts of 2,000+ tokens with 4+ Human:/Assistant: markers (A8); shared message prefix with an earlier conversation (A9).
detect_cli: Transcript entry uuids shared with earlier sessions (A9 needs CLI uuids); otherwise gateway signal.
fix_api: Class 0 alert; no corpus algorithm. DevX proposal: hash paragraphs at the gateway and warn with a suggested CLAUDE.md or memory note.
fix_cli: Move repeated background into CLAUDE.md or path-scoped rules (target under 200 lines); fork with /fork, whose first request reads the parent's cache; use a handoff file instead of pasting transcripts.

techniques.name: Fork inherits parent prefix
techniques.how: A fork keeps the parent's system prompt, tools and history exactly, so its first request reads the parent's cache; /fork copies add isolation text at the end only.
techniques.loses: Forks still replay the parent history; subagents do not inherit it.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching (Anthropic)

techniques.name: CLAUDE.md under 200 lines + path-scoped rules
techniques.how: Instructions loaded once per session; rules with paths: load on demand; survives /compact by re-read from disk.
techniques.loses: Loaded every session; long files reduce adherence.
techniques.paper: How Claude remembers your project (Anthropic)

techniques.name: Handoff file
techniques.how: Replace pasted transcripts with a short curated file the next thread reads.
techniques.loses: Hand-maintained.
techniques.paper: Context Management Across Codex Surfaces (Developer Toolkit)

methodology: Count duplicated tokens per project before and after moving background to CLAUDE.md; check task success unchanged.
gaps: No corpus source for dedup of pasted text; the thresholds are hermes's own, unsupported.

name: Compaction cost
why: Compaction writes a summary (an LLM call) and the next turn rewrites the cache from scratch.
detect_api: Gateway: sudden context drop plus cache_creation spike on the following request; summary call visible as a separate request. Cost = summary output tokens plus the rewrite premium.
detect_cli: PreCompact/PostCompact hooks with trigger manual or auto (C:074); compact_boundary entries in transcripts.
fix_api: Set compact trigger high enough that it fires rarely (default 150K, minimum 50K) and supply `instructions` so one pass keeps the right facts; prefer clearing for re-fetchable results. Class 2.
fix_cli: Codex: model_auto_compact_token_limit (clamped to 90% of window) and experimental_compact_prompt_file; Claude Code: PreCompact hook, Compact Instructions, idleCompaction=false; count compactions and restart at three.

techniques.name: Server-side compaction (compact_20260112)
techniques.how: Beta context edit that fires at `trigger` (default 150K, minimum 50K), summarises the conversation into a typed compaction block, accepts custom `instructions` and `pause_after_compaction`.
techniques.effect: Cookbook: peak 335,279 to 169,164 tokens with a 2,783-token summary; high-level facts kept 3/3, obscure specifics 0/3. Single run. Figures are from A:271.
techniques.loses: Loses verbatim detail; next turn rebuilds the cache; on short sessions the summary call costs more than it saves.
techniques.paper: Context engineering: memory, compaction, and tool clearing (Claude cookbook)

techniques.name: Cache-warm delay rule
techniques.how: Delay compaction while the cache is warm; compact only when full-window quality loss exceeds the cache-invalidation cost. One compaction on a 125,000-token context costs $0.40, about 21 cached turns.
techniques.loses: Secondary blog; sources disagree on whether compaction destroys or reuses the cache.
techniques.paper: Context Compaction Showdown (Vaughan); How Claude Code uses prompt caching (Anthropic)

techniques.name: Codex compaction tuning
techniques.how: model_auto_compact_token_limit (effective limit min(user, 0.9 x window)) and a custom compact prompt; every compaction is an LLM call.
techniques.loses: Multiple compactions reduce accuracy; no threshold study.
techniques.paper: Mastering Context Compaction in Codex CLI (Vaughan)

methodology: Compaction break-even sweep at 50K, 100K, 200K contexts with accuracy after 1, 2 and 3 compactions (the design R3 also lists); billed cost with caching on.
gaps: Compaction threshold comparison (50% vs 90% vs window minus 33,000) has no head-to-head in the corpus.

name: Git and GitHub output
why: Full diffs, lockfile diffs, log metadata, repeated status and whole PR or issue histories are large and mostly unread, and stay in history.
detect_api: Bash tool_use matching git diff/show/log/status or gh pr/issue view; result above 4,000 tokens; lockfile sections above 500; identical git status hash twice (hermes A91-A96).
detect_cli: Gateway signal only; hook sees the command; OTel tool_result has tool_name.
fix_api: No corpus technique. DevX proposal: tool-server or gateway caps on diffs, with the agent steered to git diff --stat, --name-only, pathspec excludes for lockfiles and git log --oneline -n.
fix_cli: Claude Code PreToolUse updatedInput hook rewriting git diff/log commands to bounded forms (mechanism from A:215, command list DevX proposal). Subagent for review. Beware skills that inject full git diff HEAD or gh pr view --comments with the dynamic-context syntax.

techniques.name: PreToolUse command rewrite (updatedInput)
techniques.how: Hook inspects the Bash command and returns a bounded replacement; the doc's example does this for test runners. Applying it to git commands is a DevX proposal.
techniques.loses: Only one hook may rewrite the same input; rewritten output can hide lines the agent needs.
techniques.paper: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code); Automate actions with hooks (guide), Anthropic

techniques.name: Deterministic CLI output compression (vendor claim, unverified)
techniques.how: A commercial command-output compressor claims 75-80% savings for git diff, git log, ls and grep; the paper found only the vendor's reference literals, no paired billed run.
techniques.effect: not measured in corpus (vendor claim only).
techniques.loses: C:024 found hook compression gave -2.7% to +48.4% billed cost, so token cuts do not imply cost cuts.
techniques.paper: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction

techniques.name: Dynamic context injection and subagent delegation
techniques.how: Skills can inject command output such as git diff HEAD or gh pr diff before the model sees the skill, so size is bounded only by the command. A forked Explore or Plan agent starts without git status and CLAUDE.md to keep context small.
techniques.loses: Injected diff is unbounded unless the command is bounded.
techniques.paper: Extend Claude with skills, Anthropic

methodology: Replay traces with the rewrite on; metric billed cost per success and rate of follow-up git calls (the agent re-asking for the full diff). Hold out PR review tasks where the full diff is needed.
gaps: Corpus has no measured technique for git or GitHub output. Named git flags are DevX proposals, not from a source.

name: Dependency, vendor and generated files
why: Reads and search hits in node_modules, build output, lockfiles and generated code add tokens with no task value and widen later searches.
detect_api: Read path or search result lines (5 or more) matching node_modules, .venv, dist, build, target, vendor, __pycache__, or generated patterns (.lock, .min.js, .map, _pb2.py) in tool_use input and result (hermes A76, A77).
detect_cli: Gateway signal only; PreToolUse hook sees file_path.
fix_api: No gateway technique in corpus. DevX proposal: strip dependency-path results from tool output in the tool server and alert on first hit.
fix_cli: Claude Code: permissions.deny Read rules for dist, build, generated and vendor paths in .claude/settings.json (searches already respect .gitignore); a Read deny rule does not stop a Bash grep -r. Blog also claims a .claudeignore, not in the official doc.

techniques.name: permissions.deny Read rules
techniques.how: Add rules such as Read(./**/dist/**/*) and Read(./**/vendor/**/*) to .claude/settings.json; the built-in Grep and Glob omit denied paths on a best-effort basis, and file commands in Bash are covered.
techniques.loses: A Bash grep -r over a directory with denied files still includes them; subprocesses that open files are not covered.
techniques.paper: Set up Claude Code in a monorepo or large codebase, Anthropic

techniques.name: Respect .gitignore in content search
techniques.how: Claude Code content searches skip paths in .gitignore (node_modules, dist, build) with no configuration.
techniques.loses: Only for ignored paths; checked-in vendor code needs deny rules.
techniques.paper: Set up Claude Code in a monorepo or large codebase, Anthropic

techniques.name: .claudeignore exclusion list (blog claim)
techniques.how: Blog lists node_modules, build, dist, .venv, vendor, *.lock, *.min.js, generated and __pycache__ for exclusion.
techniques.effect: Blog claims about 60% less context retrieval; no method given, unverified.
techniques.loses: Official doc in corpus does not mention .claudeignore; use permissions.deny.
techniques.paper: Claude Code Cost Optimization: A Benchmark-Backed Playbook for Cutting Token Spend (blog)

techniques.name: Cline strict path filtering (failure description)
techniques.how: Cline docs describe directory listings and searches without strict path filtering pulling node_modules, target and dist trees into history.
techniques.loses: Description only, no fix measured.
techniques.paper: How to Monitor and Optimize Token Usage in Cline

methodology: Before enabling deny rules, count how often the dependency reads were followed by an edit to that path (should be near zero). Then paired run, billed cost per success and a check that no task needed the denied path.
gaps: No measured saving from an official source. No Codex or Kiro ignore setting in the corpus. API-agent gateway fix is a DevX proposal.

name: Verbose agent reports and briefs
why: A long helper report re-enters the parent context and is re-billed every later turn.
detect_api: Response size of helper-shaped conversation versus the next parent request growth.
detect_cli: SubagentStop output tokens; parent context growth after return.
fix_api: Truncate or summarize helper results at gateway (observation masking); cap output tokens.
fix_cli: Prompt cap such as Max 30 lines; short summaries back; maxTurns; tool_output_token_limit (25k default).

techniques.name: Report length cap in prompt
techniques.how: Instruct the helper to return at most 30 lines or a 1,000-2,000 token summary.
techniques.loses: Summary may drop detail.
techniques.paper: Claude Code docs and best practices; context engineering guide

techniques.name: tool_output_token_limit
techniques.how: Caps tool result size; 25k default.
techniques.loses: Truncated results can hide needed data.
techniques.paper: Codex config docs; tool design guide

techniques.name: Observation masking (M=10)
techniques.how: Replace old observations beyond the last M=10 with placeholders.
techniques.effect: See source; summaries mask failure signals.
techniques.loses: Hides failure signals.
techniques.paper: C:130 trajectory elongation study

methodology: Compare parent cost and pass rate with cap versus without on matched tasks.
gaps: No measured effect of report caps.

name: Repeated reads of unchanged files
why: The same file is read again with no edit between, so a second copy of its tokens is added to history and re-billed each turn.
detect_api: Same Read (path, offset, limit) in tool_use input twice with no Edit/Write of that path between; duplicate tool_result tokens (hermes A72). Cross-agent re-reads need helper identity (row 24 style, C).
detect_cli: Hook transcript gives agent id for cross-agent repeats; OTel tool_result and PostToolUse give path. Gateway signal for same-agent repeats.
fix_api: Alert. Repeat-read stub ('unchanged since turn N') at a gateway is a DevX proposal and edits history, so apply at ingestion only. For old copies use clear_tool_uses; keep reads out of the main thread with subagents.
fix_cli: Claude Code: DevSkills principle (reuse context, justify re-reads) in a skill or CLAUDE.md; durable facts in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md so they survive compaction; Codex lower tool_output_token_limit. Claude Code appends a system-reminder on file change.

techniques.name: DevSkills anti-repetition principles (SubRetrv, ReTest)
techniques.how: Seven principles: state a hypothesis before retrieval, reuse context, justify re-reads, rerun tests only when code or evidence changes, break unproductive loops.
techniques.effect: Cost cut 7.88-41.73% in 6 of 8 settings; subsumed retrieval is 5.01-11.41% of cost, test re-execution up to 5.39%.
techniques.loses: One setting lost 1.5 pp Pass@1; replicate locally.
techniques.paper: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents

techniques.name: Observation masking
techniques.how: Older tool observations, including earlier copies of a file, are replaced by a placeholder outside a rolling window of M turns.
techniques.effect: M=10: -56.1% cost (Gemini 2.5 Flash); loses at 7 events or fewer (-45% to -149%).
techniques.loses: Edits history so it breaks the cache unless applied at a trigger.
techniques.paper: The Complexity Trap (JetBrains Research); Evaluating Memory Condensation Strategies for Coding Agents

techniques.name: TokenEconomizer micro-skill injection
techniques.how: An external controller learns repeated per-repository actions and injects operational micro-skills so facts are not rediscovered; key for a repeated action is the normalised command's first 6 tokens or tool plus file base name.
techniques.effect: Average cost -18.4 to -30.9% overall; micro-skills alone -11.8% and -14.3% in Claude Code settings.
techniques.loses: Learned over a task stream, costs more on early tasks, comparable success only.
techniques.paper: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents (Li et al., UC Berkeley and Microsoft Research)

techniques.name: Persistent project memory (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)
techniques.how: Facts that must survive compaction belong in AGENTS.md, which Codex re-reads at session start and after compaction, instead of in re-read files.
techniques.loses: Codex AGENTS.md truncates at 32 KiB; Claude Code advice is under 200 lines.
techniques.paper: Mastering Context Compaction in Codex CLI; Codex Context Management: Auto-Compact and /context (blogs)

methodology: Detector first on matched history. Then A/B with the DevSkills text (A:059 design: held-out tasks, repeats, Pass@1 tracked) and report re-read count, billed cost per success and Pass@1. Test masking window M at 5, 10, 20.
gaps: No corpus implementation of a gateway repeat-read stub or measured cache impact of one. No Kiro or Aider re-read control in corpus.

name: Re-learning the codebase
why: Each session re-reads the same files before first edit because what earlier sessions learned was never saved.
detect_api: Gateway: Read tool_use paths before the first edit, seen in 2+ earlier conversations of the same project (needs project key from caller/header).
detect_cli: Transcript/hook Read paths per project across sessions; PostToolUse hook gives tool_input.file_path (C:074).
fix_api: Class 0 alert; recommend a memory file. Gateway cannot save notes.
fix_cli: Enable auto memory (autoMemoryEnabled) and CLAUDE.md; Aider repo map (tree-sitter + PageRank, --map-tokens budget) gives a ranked symbol map instead of re-exploring; TokenEconomizer micro-skills.

techniques.name: TokenEconomizer experience micro-skills
techniques.how: Learns repository facts (commands, test invocations, edited files) from earlier trajectories and injects them as micro-skills confirmed across non-overlapping tasks.
techniques.effect: Tokens down 18.4-30.9%; micro-skill injection alone -11.8% and -14.3% in two Claude Code settings.
techniques.loses: Skills go stale; cost rises on first tasks.
techniques.paper: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents (TokenEconomizer)

techniques.name: Memory tool and notes (memory_20250818)
techniques.how: Agent writes /memories files and views them in later sessions.
techniques.effect: Session 2 with memory: peak 172,623 tokens vs 333,977 without (reads 4 of 8 documents). Single synthetic run.
techniques.loses: Notes can go out of date; Pokemon example shows over-writing makes recall costly.
techniques.paper: Context engineering cookbook; The components of agent memory (Anthropic)

techniques.name: Aider repo map
techniques.how: Tree-sitter extracts symbols, a graph is ranked with a PageRank variant, and the top symbols are emitted within a token budget (default 1k, up to 4k for large repos).
techniques.effect: Built in 0.4 s cold; token saving not measured.
techniques.loses: Standing charge sent every turn; may omit what the task needs.
techniques.paper: Claude Code vs Aider benchmarks (C:041); How to Reduce Aider Token Usage (C:127)

methodology: Sequential task stream per repo as in C:028: with vs without memory/micro-skills, tokens before first edit, pass@1 within 3 points.
gaps: Corpus has no per-file exploration cost figure; savings from CLAUDE.md alone are not measured.

name: High effort on trivial turns
why: Reasoning tokens are billed as output; a trivial reply with thousands of reasoning tokens wastes the highest-priced tokens.
detect_api: One call, no tools, reply 300 tokens or fewer, output minus reply over 3,000 tokens; cost (reasoning - 1,000) * out_price.
detect_cli: Transcript usage per turn plus effort setting; same signature on short chat turns.
fix_api: Class 2 after a paired win: set output_config.effort per request (low for simple turns); per-message effort keeps the cache. max_tokens as hard limit with adaptive thinking.
fix_cli: effortLevel setting, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL env var, --effort flag; maxEffortLevel as managed cap. Codex: model_reasoning_effort.

techniques.name: Effort parameter
techniques.how: output_config.effort low to max governs thinking, text and tool calls; per-message effort preserves the prompt cache.
techniques.loses: Behavioural signal; run an effort sweep.
techniques.paper: Effort parameter (Claude); extended thinking tips

techniques.name: Prompt-Induced Waste (effort arm)
techniques.how: Paired comparison of effort, prompt and harness on cost per successful task.
techniques.effect: Effort-only arm gave 91% of the full-stack reduction (about 75% under DeepSeek Harness vs about 19% in Claude Code).
techniques.loses: Effort can add cost without benefit or help on hard tasks.
techniques.paper: Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents

techniques.name: Overthinking evidence
techniques.how: o1-like models use 1,953% more tokens on 2+3; self-training cuts output 48.6%.
techniques.loses: Needs training; not a gateway fix.
techniques.paper: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=?

methodology: Paired bootstrap, McNemar and Holm on cost per successful task, per C:026, across effort levels.
gaps: NoWait (A:091) and ALP (A:096) need decoding or training control, not available at a gateway. Codex multipliers (C:105) are community estimates.

name: Tool discovery and skill loading
why: Repeated ToolSearch calls and skill file reads add tokens; big invoked skill bodies are charged until compaction.
detect_api: Gateway signal only: tool_use names for ToolSearch above 2 per conversation key.
detect_cli: Hook events: ToolSearch calls beyond 2 per session; Read of /skills/ paths not ending SKILL.md; invoked skill bodies above 3k tokens.
fix_api: Keep a stable wrapper (get_tool_schema/invoke_tool) so discovery is one step. Class 0.
fix_cli: Trim skill descriptions (capped at 1,536 characters), set skillOverrides to name-only, or disable-model-invocation on rare skills. Class 3.

techniques.name: skillOverrides and disable-model-invocation
techniques.how: States on, name-only, user-invocable-only, off; disable-model-invocation keeps a skill out of context until /name.
techniques.loses: Model can no longer auto-invoke.
techniques.paper: Claude Code, Extend Claude with skills; Anthropic, Explore the context window

techniques.name: Skill re-attach budget
techniques.how: After compaction invoked skills return at 5,000 tokens each, 25,000 total, most recent first.
techniques.loses: Large skills consume the budget.
techniques.paper: Claude Code, Extend Claude with skills

techniques.name: On-demand schema access
techniques.how: get_tool_schema/invoke_tool proxy keeps a stable wrapper, cache-friendly.
techniques.loses: Namespacing prefixes.
techniques.paper: Atlassian, MCP Compression

methodology: Count ToolSearch and skill reads per session before and after trimming; guard on task success.
gaps: No corpus source for the A:65 ToolSearch threshold; DevX proposal.

name: Usage while idle
why: Prompts fired with no human hook activity (loops, scheduled reruns) keep spending tokens while nobody is working.
detect_api: Gateway sees only timing and regularity: fixed-interval or off-hours calls with identical prefix. A138 flags cross-session scheduled reruns.
detect_cli: Hook data: prompts with no hook record within 15 seconds, counted only after the first hook record.
fix_api: Class 0 alert with budget alerts. DevX proposal: per-key schedule rate limit.
fix_cli: Class 3: stop or schedule the loop; Claude Code idleCompaction setting (v2.1.290+) compacts idle one-hour-TTL conversations. Handoff file moves a task between threads.

techniques.name: Idle compaction
techniques.how: After idle on the one-hour TTL, Claude Code can compact the conversation; idleCompaction false turns it off.
techniques.loses: Compaction rewrites the prefix and costs a cache miss.
techniques.paper: How Claude Code uses prompt caching

techniques.name: Handoff file
techniques.how: A handoff file and two prompts move a task between threads without re-planning.
techniques.loses: Manual discipline.
techniques.paper: Context Management Across Codex Surfaces

techniques.name: Budget alerts
techniques.how: Alerts at 75%, 90% and 100% of a set budget.
techniques.loses: Alerts, not enforcement; Copilot premium-request scope.
techniques.paper: Overview of request-based billing (legacy)

methodology: Backtest the 15-second no-hook rule on recorded sessions and review flagged prompts manually before alerting.
gaps: no corpus source for detecting idle usage at a gateway; A:053 and hook docs not opened. DevX proposal: regularity (fixed-interval) detector.

name: MCP tool schema bloat
why: Every unused mcp__ tool definition is re-read each call; median session carries about 91k tokens of MCP definitions.
detect_api: Hash and size of tools[] by namespace prefix; flag tools never called.
detect_cli: prompt_snapshot.tools[] versus tool_use calls per server; /context.
fix_api: Replace schemas with a compressing MCP proxy (get_tool_schema/invoke_tool). Class 2.
fix_cli: Disable rarely used servers (class 3); in Codex use enabled_tools or disabled_tools allow/deny lists.

techniques.name: mcp-compressor
techniques.how: MCP proxy replacing tools with get_tool_schema/invoke_tool.
techniques.loses: Quality depends on on-demand schema access.
techniques.paper: Atlassian, MCP Compression

techniques.name: Server disable and Codex tool allow/deny lists
techniques.how: mcp_servers.<id>.enabled, enabled_tools, disabled_tools applied after enabled_tools; omit tools from direct, deferred or code_mode surfaces.
techniques.effect: GitHub MCP with 93 tools is about 55,000 tokens per turn.
techniques.loses: Loses the disabled tools.
techniques.paper: Codex configuration reference; Vaughan, Codex CLI Performance Optimisation

techniques.name: Code execution mode and mcp2cli
techniques.how: Code-mode tool calls and CLI list/help lookups at about 16 and 120 tokens per tool.

techniques.loses: Redesign effort.

detect_cli: skill_listing and agent_listing_delta entries versus Skill invocations.
fix_api: Not applicable at the gateway; alert only. Class 0.
fix_cli: Retire stale skills, set skillOverrides off or name-only, disableBundledSkills. Class 3.

techniques.loses: Imports do not reduce cost.

techniques.loses: Still cost tokens each call.

name: No visibility
why: Sessions with no hook or telemetry data leave categories, ratings and idle time unknown; a coverage gap, not a cost.
detect_api: Gateway: share of requests with no caller key, session or project tag header; share of traffic that bypasses the gateway.
detect_cli: Share of gateway sessions (x-claude-code-session-id) with no matching hook or OTel rows.
fix_api: Require a virtual key per developer/team and a metadata header per request; ship events to Langfuse as a sidecar.
fix_cli: Claude Code: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 with OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER/OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER in managed settings (locked); hooks via allowManagedHooksOnly; Codex: [otel] exporter keys and hooks in config.toml (user-level, project-local otel is ignored).

techniques.name: Claude Code OpenTelemetry
techniques.how: Telemetry flag plus exporters emits token and cost metrics and events tagged with session.id (OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID); admin can lock exporters in managed settings; prompt text is redacted unless OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1.
techniques.loses: A developer can still set selectors to console or none unless managed settings lock them.
techniques.paper: Monitoring usage (Claude Code OpenTelemetry) (Anthropic)

techniques.name: Gateway tagging with session header
techniques.how: Gateway on the request path records tokens/cost per request tagged to developer and team; Claude Code sends x-claude-code-session-id on every request; headers prefixed x-bf-lh- are copied to log metadata.
techniques.loses: Needs the developer to route via the gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL).
techniques.paper: Claude Code Token Usage: Monitor It with an AI Gateway; Run Claude Code through a gateway

techniques.name: Managed hooks and Langfuse coding-agent tracing
techniques.how: allowManagedHooksOnly and managed hooks cannot be disabled by user settings; Langfuse traces every agent LLM call via hooks or a gateway, per team, repository and model.
techniques.loses: Hooks need harness support; unmanaged hooks can be disabled.
techniques.paper: Hooks reference (Anthropic); Track and optimize coding agent usage (Langfuse)

methodology: Coverage audit: ratio of sessions with hook/OTel rows to gateway sessions, per harness and version; target set from the P0 baseline.
gaps: Corpus does not say what coverage share is adequate.
